title: DNA Data Storage
summary: Storing digital data as synthesised DNA strands, offering extreme density and century-scale durability.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

DNA data storage encodes binary files as sequences of the four DNA bases, synthesises the strands, and reads them back with sequencing. The theoretical density is orders of magnitude higher than tape or optical media, and dry DNA can survive for centuries.

Where It Stands

Write and read costs remain far above archival tape, and random access requires careful indexing. Research systems have demonstrated full round trips at the megabyte scale, but throughput is measured in bytes per second rather than megabytes.

What Would Change It

Cheaper enzymatic synthesis, faster nanopore sequencing and a workable random-access scheme. The first commercial niche is likely compliance archives that must outlive any current storage medium, not hot data.

businessMeaning: Only worth a pilot where retention is measured in decades and rewriting is rare: regulated archives, scientific records and media masters. Compare cost per gigabyte-decade, not cost per gigabyte.
investmentLens: No pure listed exposure. Watch DNA synthesis suppliers and archival storage incumbents for the first paid deployments.
